svg.title: DSpark and DFlash-style training attention: flexible boundaries and partial sparsity
svg.desc: A toy packed score matrix with five anchors across two documents. Each anchor owns seven query rows. Visible keys are its document context strictly before its anchor and its complete seven-by-seven draft block. Other document and other draft blocks are hidden. Empty tiles can be skipped, full tiles can run without a score predicate, and partial tiles require exact score masking.
svg.metadata: Original ASpec explanatory artwork. Copyright 2026 Ant Group Co., Ltd. SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0. Toy lengths and inspection windows; not a measured GPU tile layout.
svg.text: Each anchor expands B=7 query rows: a document prefix plus one complete 7×7 draft block.
Visible keys = [document context start, anchor) ∪ [own draft start, own draft end)
This needs a flexible mask, while whole empty tiles provide an opportunity to skip work.
No QK / PV MMA for this tile.
A bit marks a visible score; it does not make a dense MMA instruction skip individual masked multiplications.
Mask shown: full attention within each draft block, no extra sliding window, all anchors valid.
Toy document lengths and inspection windows are for illustration; they are not the benchmark lengths or GPU tile geometry.
